title: Chapter 71 — Defending the Book: Competitive Defence
intro: Thinking like your attacker and preventing churn.

sections.title: Defence Is Proactive
sections.content:
Do not wait for a competitor to take your account. Anticipate where they will attack — price, service, product availability — and shore up those areas before they get the chance.

The best defence is consistent excellence. Accounts that receive outstanding service rarely switch for a slightly lower price.

sections.title: Coaching Rule
sections.content:
When evaluating competitive defence, ask:

Is the salesperson aware of competitive threats to their accounts?
Are they proactively strengthening relationships — or taking them for granted?
Is churn happening — and if so, why?
